requirements.requirement: Something to keep sewing supplies tidy (organized storage)
requirements.evidence: 3-cell cluster (piece:0,0,0;full + 0,1,0 + 1,0,0) with bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full (large open bin for fabric/spools), bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments for notions/buttons), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments for tools). Provides 6 organized compartments plus large bin.

Workshop props placed: tweezers (as small sewing scissors proxy) visible, heap-screws-div3 (buttons/notions proxy) placed but below rim warning. No dedicated sewing props (thread spools, fabric, scissors, needles) exist in catalog - filament-spool and tape too large for compartments, so generic small-part props used.

finish.summary: Built compact 3-cell sewing organizer: one large full-depth bin for bulk items and two divided bins (3-way + 2-way) giving 6 compartments for thread, buttons, needles etc. Capped and bolted. Dressed with available small props to show organization; dedicated sewing props not in catalog.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your sewing kit deserves its own tidy station — I'll put together a compact organizer for it.
